question: Explain why energy is released in nuclear fission and nuclear fusion. Use the concept of binding energy per nucleon to justify your answer.

options.A: Fission and fusion release energy because their products have lower binding energy per nucleon and higher total mass than the initial nuclei.
options.B: Only fission releases energy because fusion always lowers binding energy per nucleon.
options.C: In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into medium-mass nuclei; in fusion, light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus. In both cases the final nuclei have greater binding energy per nucleon and lower total mass, so the increase in binding energy is released as $E=\Delta mc^2$.
options.D: Fission and fusion release energy because all nucleons vanish during the reactions.
